page: List of tallest buildings in Vancouver

rows.text: 2nd tallest building in British Columbia and 39th tallest building in Canada. Contains a hotel on the first 15 floors and residential units on the rest of the tower. Will soon rebrand to the Hyatt Vancouver Downtown Alberni. Tallest building completed in Vancouver in the 2000s.
rows.link: List of tallest buildings in British Columbia

rows.text: Tied with Altus in Burnaby for the third tallest building in British Columbia. Tallest building completed in Vancouver in the 2010s. Mixed-use hotel and residential building.
Tallest building completed in Vancouver in the 2020s.
The Private Residences at Hotel Georgia
667 Howe Street 49°17′02″N 123°07′07″W / 49.283787°N 123.11869°W / 49.283787; -123.11869 (The Private Residences at Hotel Georgia)
Features a top-heavy design that is unique in Vancouver.
This building is also known as the Sheraton Wall Centre. Tallest building in Vancouver from 2001 to 2009.
Tallest building in Vancouver from 1977 to 2001. Tallest office building in the city from 1977 to 2023. Tallest building completed in Vancouver in the 1970s.
Seeking Platinum LEED certification, will be Gold LEED at least.
Tallest all-residential tower in Vancouver. The building also has the tallest rooftop pool in the city.
Tallest building in Vancouver from 1973 to 1977. Also known as the RBC Tower or Royal Bank Tower.
Largest office building in British Columbia by floor area, with 64,856 square metres (698,104 sq ft). Tallest building completed in Vancouver in the 1980s.
Also known as 200 Granville Square. The roof of the building features Vancouver Harbour Control Tower, the highest air traffic control tower in the world.
LEED Platinum for Office Building and LEED Gold certification for Residential Tower as part of the new downtown Telus headquarters project.
This building is also known as the Toronto Dominion Tower. Briefly the tallest building in Vancouver from 1972 to 1973.
The Stories at South Granville Station
1477 West Broadway 49°15′50″N 123°08′17″W / 49.26391°N 123.13817°W / 49.26391; -123.13817 (The Stories at South Granville Station)
This building is also known as W43 or the W Building.
Also known as the Bank of Montreal Tower.
This building is also known as Beach Crescent - West One.
Tallest building completed in Vancouver in the 1990s.
Sheraton Wall Centre Hotel - West Tower
1088 Burrard Street 49°16′49″N 123°07′38″W / 49.28019°N 123.127129°W / 49.28019; -123.127129 (Sheraton Wall Centre Hotel - West Tower)
Tallest building in Vancouver from 1939 to 1972. Tallest building completed in Vancouver in the 1930s.
This building is also known as the Hyatt Regency Hotel or the Hyatt Regency Vancouver-Royal Centre.
The first building in Vancouver exceeding 100 metres (328 ft) in height that is located outside of Downtown Vancouver.
Also known as Marina Pointe - Landmark 33.
Also known as 1177 West Hastings at Columbia Centre. Tallest building completed in Vancouver in the 1960s.
Originally known as the MacMillan Bloedel Building.
This building is also known as Marina Crescent - Quay West I or QuayWest I at Concord Pacific Place.
Formerly known as the Terasen Centre and was previously the site of the Rayonier Building (originally known as the Alaska White Pine Building) from 1954 to 1990.
This building is also known as Canaccord Place or 609 Granville at Pacific Centre.

rows.text: This building was the tallest free standing hotel in the city. This building was often referred to by its original name, the Sheraton Landmark. The hotel and its restaurant closed on September 30, 2017, and the building was demolished, floor by floor between March 2018 and May 2019.
